intent: Make PR CI-health rebase recovery fail closed on proven repository push authority rather than treating the mere presence of a configured secret as sufficient authority.

negative_controls.name: removing-push-authority-query-breaks-binding-test
negative_controls.command: python3 -c "from pathlib import Path; import subprocess,sys; p=Path('.github/workflows/pr-ci-health.yml'); t=p.read_text(); old='.permissions.push // false'; assert old in t; p.write_text(t.replace(old,'.permissions.admin // false',1)); r=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pytest','-q','tests/test_pr_ci_health.py::test_workflow_validates_push_authority_before_rebase'],check=False); sys.exit(r.returncode)"

interface_mismatches: The workflow maps secret presence to trusted push authority, but live run 30018083147 proved the configured fallback token authenticates without repository write permission and every attempted rebase push fails with HTTP 403.
honest_blockers: A dedicated PR_CI_HEALTH_PUSH_TOKEN has been provisioned from the operator's valid OAuth keyring credential to restore the lane immediately; its repo/workflow scope is broader than the preferred fine-grained contents-write-only credential and should be replaced when that dedicated credential is available.
The repository API permission probe proves current repository push authorization, not future validity, workflow-trigger semantics, or least-privilege scope.
Hosted exact-head CI, a second live rebase run, independent review, and human merge authority remain required.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the workflow, regression test, and this packet together. Secret presence then again becomes the only recovery-authority signal, which can produce repeated 403 push attempts.
